description: Polina Lemenkova and Abdullah Can Zülfikar at Istanbul Technical University publish OpenSeesPy simulations and a machine-learning surrogate for reinforced-concrete frames representative of Istanbul. Sixty two-dimensional frame archetypes are analysed using thirty recorded ground motions at six intensity levels, producing a 10,800-row simulation database included in the repository. Python scripts estimate drift, damage states and lognormal fragility parameters with credible intervals. The August 2026 release is free: code uses MIT, while data and figures use CC BY 4.0. Third-party inputs retain separate terms. Ground-motion waveforms and two SMD-TR tables are not redistributed; reproducing the full campaign requires obtaining them separately. Temporal coverage is scenario-based; the metadata do not identify a continuous observation period. This model can support building-risk simulations within its archetype assumptions. OpenSees is a related catalogue model; the reported numerical performance was not independently tested.
